title.narrative: Improving Gender-Based Violence responses and Coordination in Lao PDR

description.narrative: This program aims to improve social and health services for Gender-Based Violence (GBV) responses and coordination, including creating referral pathways for survivors of violence in Laos, particularly in Bokeo and Savannakhet provinces, and Vientiane capital.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: Title: From Silence to Strength – Xieng Khouang Province ‍ Namfa (pseudonym), a 16-year-old ethnic Hmong girl, was married through traditional customs to Saiphon (pseudonym), whose substance abuse led to frequent domestic conflict. In 2024, during a local festival, Namfa was assaulted by Saiphon, causing serious injuries. ‍ Police intervened, and Saiphon was arrested. The Provincial Women’s Union, with support from UNFPA and the Counselling and Protection Center, ensured Namfa received urgent medical care and psychosocial support. She was hospitalised for over ten days and later enrolled in a beauty care vocational program. This training was made possible through financial assistance from the Australia-funded UNFPA initiative, which also covered her medical expenses. Upon graduation, she gained financial independence as a professional salon worker. ‍ Legal proceedings were swift. The Xieng Khouang Provincial Court sentenced Saiphon to three years and six months in prison, issuing him a fine and awarding Namfa damages. ‍ This case highlights the effectiveness of a coordinated, multi-sectoral response to gender-based violence, combining health care, legal action, and economic empowerment. It underscores the growing commitment — with strong support from partners like Australia — to justice and protection for women and girls in Laos.
